definitions.explanation: A technical measurement of how deep something is, used in geology for earthquake depth, in oceanography for sea depth, and in photography for depth of field.

examples.japanese: ⟦{水深|すいしん}→水深：18675_suishin⟧{深度|しんど}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{計測|けいそく}→計測：14189_keisoku⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
⟦{震源|しんげん}→震源：16060_shingen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{深度|しんど}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{約|やく}→約：09563_yaku⟧10⟦キロメートル→キロメートル：02873_kiromeetoru⟧だった。
examples.english: The depth of the earthquake's epicenter was about 10 kilometers.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{湖|みずうみ}→湖：00867_mizuumi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{最大|さいだい}→最大：04827_saidai⟧{深度|しんど}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧400⟦メートル→メートル：02975_meetoru⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{超|こ}え→超える：01942_koeru⟧、⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{最|もっと}も→最も：01736_mottomo⟧⟦{深|ふか}い→深い：01211_fukai⟧⟦{湖|みずうみ}→湖：00867_mizuumi⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{知|し}られている→知る：00458_shiru⟧。
examples.english: This lake has a maximum depth exceeding 400 meters and is known as the deepest lake in Japan.

notes:
A technical or formal term for the measurement of depth, especially in scientific and geographic contexts. Combines {深|しん} (deep) and ⟦{度|ど}→〜度：09845_do⟧ (degree, measure).

USAGE:
- Used as a measurable quantity — how deep something is, expressed numerically
- Common in geology (earthquake depth), oceanography (sea depth), and photography (depth of field)
- Not to be confused with the homophone ⟦{進度|しんど}→進度：21583_shindo⟧ (degree of progress) or ⟦{震度|しんど}→震度：22807_shindo⟧ (seismic intensity)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{震源|しんげん}→震源：16060_shingen⟧{深度|しんど}: depth of earthquake hypocenter
- ⟦{最大|さいだい}→最大：04827_saidai⟧{深度|しんど}: maximum depth
- {被写界|ひしゃかい}{深度|しんど}: depth of field (photography)
- {深度|しんど}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{測|はか}る→測る：01977_hakaru⟧: to measure depth

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{深|ふか}さ→深さ：05328_fukasa⟧: depth — the everyday word for how deep something is
- ⟦{水深|すいしん}→水深：18675_suishin⟧: water depth — specifically for bodies of water
- ⟦{奥行|おくゆ}き→奥行き：10569_okuyuki⟧: depth, perspective — spatial depth of a physical space or object
